## Verifier: **pass**

I started the app myself (`mvn -B -ntp spring-boot:run` after `source .factory/sandbox/.runtime.env`; no `app.json` was present) and exercised every acceptance check over HTTP and in Chromium. Evidence is in `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/media/`.

### Acceptance checks

| \# | Check | Observed | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `/borrowers/overdue?on=2026-11-30` | `[{"borrower":"ada","overdueLoans":2,"totalDaysLate":28},{"borrower":"alan","overdueLoans":1,"totalDaysLate":12},{"borrower":"grace","overdueLoans":1,"totalDaysLate":5}]` — byte-identical to the spec | `check1-borrowers-2026-11-30.{json,png}` |
| 2 | `?on=2026-11-20` | `[{"borrower":"ada","overdueLoans":1,"totalDaysLate":10},{"borrower":"alan","overdueLoans":1,"totalDaysLate":2}]` — grace absent, ada counts 1 | `check2-borrowers-2026-11-20.{json,png}` |
| 3 | `?on=2026-11-10` | `[]` — a loan is not overdue on its due day | `check3-borrowers-2026-11-10.{json,png}` |
| 4 | bare `/borrowers/overdue` | `HTTP/1.1 200`, `Content-Type: application/json`, body a JSON array | `check4-borrowers-bare.{json,png}`, `check4-headers.txt` |
| 5 | `/loans/overdue` unchanged | `?on=2026-11-20` returns the pinned two-loan list; `?on=2026-11-10` returns `[]`. Both byte-identical to the runbook | `check5-loans-2026-11-20.{json,png}`, `check5-loans-2026-11-10.{json,png}` |

The ada row in check 1 is corroborated against the per-loan view: `/loans/overdue?on=2026-11-30` lists The Dispossessed at 20 and A Wizard of Earthsea at 8, which is exactly the 2 / 28 row (`probe-loans-2026-11-30.json`).

### Ways it could have looked right and wasn't

- **Grouping order.** `Collectors.groupingBy` returns a `HashMap`, so I called `?on=2026-11-30` ten times and got one unique response (`probe-determinism.txt`). The explicit borrower-name tie-break is in the comparator; no two borrowers can tie on any day with this data, so that branch is not observable over HTTP.
- **The second due date.** On `2026-11-22` ada is 1 loan / 12 days; on `2026-11-23` she is 2 loans / 14. The due-day boundary holds for the new loan as well as the old one.
- **Empty and saturated cases.** `?on=2026-01-01` returns `[]`; `?on=2027-01-01` returns all three borrowers with all 4 loans accounted for.
- **Error case.** `?on=not-a-date` returns `400`, the same shape the existing endpoint returns. `?on=` (empty) returns `200`, matching `/loans/overdue?on=`.
- **Default clock agrees across endpoints.** Bare `/borrowers/overdue` gave ada 1/11 and alan 1/3; bare `/loans/overdue` gave ada 11 and alan 3 on the same run.
- **Routes.** `POST` returns `405`; a repeated `on=` parameter takes the first value and still answers correctly; `localhost` works; a trailing slash is `404` — and so is `/loans/overdue/`, so that is pre-existing Spring behaviour, not something this change introduced.
- **Browser.** Chromium renders each response. The only console entry is a `favicon.ico` 404, which this app has always produced (it serves no static resources). The network panel shows the single `200` (`check1-console.txt`, `check1-network.txt`).

### Notes

- `mvn -B -ntp test` reported `Tests run: 6, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`, and all three declared tests are present in `LoanControllerTest`. Recorded for completeness only — the verdict above rests on the running app, not the suite.
- Nothing in `capabilities.not_exercised` blocked a check. Check 4 touches the clock-dependent default, but it pins only the status code and that the body is an array, both of which I exercised directly. No `sandbox-report.json` was written.
- The app was stopped and `target/` removed afterwards. The workspace is clean apart from a pre-existing uncommitted `.gitignore` edit (adding `.playwright-cli/`) that was already there when I started.
